text:
LANDING REQUEST - scout ACCEPT is in at post-01M17QV6KEBTWEGTEC95923V19, hold released, no second
finding. bd-01M177SHFXZKMR8K39BPC9K6FF.

SHA TO GATE: 9952ab2 on m1/chart-eligibility, base 451221b (current main).

WHY NOT THE SHA SCOUT ACCEPTED: main moved to 451221b after their review. 9952ab2 is 6e57168 rebased
onto it. `git diff 6e57168..9952ab2 -- '*.scala'` is ZERO LINES - the accepted code is byte-identical
and only the base moved (451221b is your AGENTS.md commit, no Scala). I re-gated on the new base
anyway rather than carrying the old numbers across the rebase.

Gate on 9952ab2: seven modules from reference-scope.sh, seven totals counted, zero failures -
align 211, codec 108, embedBench 64, embedGrakern 28, fixtures 117, interview 92, laws 86.
scalafmtCheckAll last, separately, clean.

WHAT LANDS: two files, cost.scala and CostSuite.scala. I checked this against your new rule rather
than assuming it - `git status --short` with NO pathspec on my worktree shows only my two untracked
scratch probes, and `git show --stat HEAD` lists exactly those two files. Nothing of anyone else's
is in the index. The rule is a good one and it caught a real hazard in how I have been committing:
I use `git add <paths>` then `git commit --amend`, which takes the WHOLE index, and I had been
relying on my worktree being private rather than on checking.

CONTENT, briefly: both optional evidence-backed terms are produced by reductions over
view.structuralMembers(node.ref), and neither eligibility predicate asked that population. Chart
under-claimed (tested node.evidence, the contract of a different function) and discounted segment
cells 14.9% while clamping support to a fabricated 1.0. Structural over-claimed (asked only whether
a provider was configured) and inflated chartless cells 15%. Both now consult one shared
chartedMembers val. Three mutations die, each with thirteen siblings passing:
  chartEligible reverted        support 1.0 claims nothing was assumed, but Sensory was
  structuralEligible old form   expected 0.9552238805970149 but was 0.8311688311688312
  structuralEligible = false    expected 0.9655172413793105 but was 1.0
No expected value anywhere in seven modules moved, which is the prediction the Chart fix makes.

ON THE THREE HOLDS. You said scout held three of my candidates today on things a green suite could
not show, and that each time the production fix was right while the evidence was not yet sufficient
to prove it. I want to name the specific thing I was doing wrong, because "write better tests" does
not describe it: BOTH of my controls were named for what I wanted them to prove rather than derived
from what would falsify them. The third hold is the clearest case - my charted control asserted the
term was present and the totals differed, and both survive `structuralEligible = false`, because
term production happens before eligibility is consulted. The rule I am taking is that A CONTROL MUST
NAME THE MUTATION IT KILLS. If I cannot say which edit turns it red, it is a description, not a
control. That is checkable before review rather than after, which is the point.

AFTER THIS LANDS I still owe you a sequencing answer on bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 - the semantic
abstention finding, where an abstaining provider and one measuring exactly 0.5 are bit-identical
including support. Scout's accept explicitly leaves it as a separate later candidate, which matches
my lean. I will not start it until you rule.
